summary: Focused verification of the Resident Suggestions bug fix (WhatsApp poll vote ingestion). Backend: 7/7 pytest cases pass in /app/backend/tests/test_suggestions.py — auth, create returns non-null poll_message_id (local-<uuid> as expected on 402 Whapi plan), /api/whapi/webhook with a matching poll_message_id updates yes_votes/no_votes to absolute values from poll.results (5/3 then 8/1 confirmed absolute-not-additive), unknown message-id webhooks return 200 and do not mutate other suggestions, manual dashboard vote increments yes_votes by 1, PUT status -> GET reflects, GET returns {suggestions, stats} with stats.total_votes == sum of yes+no across suggestions. Frontend Playwright: society admin login -> nav-suggestions loads Suggestions page with all four stat cards (sg-total, sg-review, sg-approved, sg-votes), filter tabs, suggestion cards with vote bars and Yes/No buttons; add-suggestion dialog creates a new suggestion which appears immediately; vote-yes-<id> increments UI from 0 -> 1; status-<id> Select updates to Approved and the badge reflects it; delete cleans up. No console errors. All created test data cleaned up.
critical_code_review_comments: _apply_poll_results treats yes/no==None as 0 when only one side is present; that is intentional given absolute-count semantics, but note it means a webhook that omits an option will zero it out. Current test env sends both, so behaviour is correct.
suggestions_router.create_suggestion never raises when Whapi returns 402 — it falls back to a local-<uuid> poll_message_id. Good defensive design; keep it.
seed_data_creation: All TEST_* suggestions were auto-deleted by the pytest module-scope teardown and the UI test explicitly deleted its created suggestion. No residual demo data.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Suggestions regression tests live in /app/backend/tests/test_suggestions.py and run in ~4s. To simulate a poll vote, POST /api/whapi/webhook (no auth) with {messages:[{id:<poll_message_id>, type:'poll', from_me:true, chat_id:'<any>@g.us', poll:{results:[{name:'Yes',count:N},{name:'No',count:M}]}}]}. Poll updates are absolute (overwrite), not additive.
rca_of_the_issue: Original bug had two parts: (a) messages were sent as a text-with-buttons question instead of a native WhatsApp poll, and (b) group votes never came back to the backend. Fix now uses Whapi POST /messages/poll (send_poll) to send a native poll and stores the returned message id (or a local- fallback on 402 plans). /api/whapi/webhook now recognises type==poll (or a poll field) and routes to _apply_poll_results, which finds the suggestion by poll_message_id and overwrites yes_votes/no_votes from poll.results counts. Verified end-to-end via 7 backend tests + Playwright UI.
